books.title: Aino Folk-Tales
books.author: Basil Hall Chamberlain
books.synopsis: Chamberlain writes down the oral tales of the Ainu of Yezo as told by chiefs and villagers, from how the owl got his feather cap to why dogs cannot speak. Fox-gods, the civilizer Okikurumi, the Panaumbe and Penaumbe cycle, a man who weds the Bear-Goddess and a hunter in Hades fill its moral tales and scraps of folklore.

books.title: Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan: First Series
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn lands in Yokohama, rides by jinricksha to Kamakura and Enoshima, then settles in Matsue to explore Izumo's shrines, festivals and village superstitions. He visits the Great Shrine of Kitzuki, the cave of the children's ghosts, and the temple at Hinomisaki, finding the living Shinto in the national heart rather than in books.

books.title: Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan: Second Series
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn continues his Matsue years with the household shrine, women's hair, a garden of frogs and lotus, ancestor worship and the Japanese smile, then sails to the remote Oki islands and the farewell of Kumamoto. Ghost-lore, Buddhist funerals, student essays and the Shinto roots of the family religion fill out a portrait of old Izumo giving way to the new Japan.

books.title: In Ghostly Japan
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Opening with a Bodhisattva's vision of a mountain made of skulls, Hearn gathers tales of the Long-sleeved Robe and the Peony-Lantern ghosts, and a fortune-teller who saves a man haunted by his dead lover. Essays follow on incense games, the footprints of the Buddha, Japanese verse and Buddhist proverbs, with a priest who meets a Tengu among the closing stories.

books.title: Japanese Fairy Tales
books.author: Yei Theodora Ozaki
books.synopsis: Twenty-two tales retold for Western children: Urashima Taro rides a tortoise to the Sea King's palace, Momotaro sets out from a peach to fight ogres, and a sparrow loses her tongue to a wicked old woman. Along the way come goblins, talking badgers and monkeys, the Bamboo-cutter's moon-child and the Empress who mends the sky with stones of five colors.

books.title: Kokoro: Hints and Echoes of Japanese Inner Life
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn turns from outward Japan to its heart, from a murderer's confrontation with his victim's child at a Kumamoto railway station to a bugler who dies sounding the charge and a cholera-time village. Long essays on karma, pre-existence and ancestor-worship set Buddhist doctrine beside Herbert Spencer and Huxley, and an appendix gives three popular ballads sung by Matsue's outcast yama-no-mono.

books.title: Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: A blind biwa-player named Hoichi is summoned each night to recite the fall of the Heike to a court of ghosts, until a priest paints the Heart Sutra over his body and forgets his ears. Snow-women, headless Rokuro-Kubi, a man-eating jikininki and a dream of a kingdom inside an ant-hill give way to Hearn's closing essays on butterflies, mosquitoes and ants.

books.title: Shadowings
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.synopsis: Hearn retells strange Japanese tales of reunited ghosts, a dreamer's vision of Fugen-Bosatsu and a painted girl who steps from her picture, then turns to essays on the shrilling of cicadas, girls' names and old street ballads. The book closes with reveries on nightmares and a mysterious dream-book that rewrites itself.

books.title: The American Diary of a Japanese Girl
books.author: Yoné Noguchi
books.synopsis: Morning Glory, a young Japanese woman, lands in San Francisco and records her wide-eyed, wisecracking adventures with her uncle, from Longfellow-loving society ladies to a cottage next door to a poet named Heine. Her broken-English diary lampoons American manners while she dreams of becoming a novelist.

books.title: The Book of Tea
books.author: Kakuzo Okakura
books.synopsis: Okakura turns the humble cup of tea into an Eastern philosophy of life, tracing Teaism from Chinese medicine to Zen-flavoured Japanese ceremony. He moves from the bare tea-room and its Taoist love of the imperfect to flower-arranging, art appreciation and the tea-master Rikiu's final tea before his suicide.

books.title: The Japanese Spirit
books.author: Yoshisaburo Okakura
books.synopsis: Okakura traces how Shinto, Confucianism, Taoism and Zen Buddhism fused into the Japanese national character, from the Samurai code and hara-kiri to the tea ceremony and the seventeen-syllable hokku. A Japanese professor explains his country to a Western audience.

books.title: The No Plays of Japan
books.author: Arthur Waley
books.synopsis: Waley's translation of twenty-odd No plays, where ghosts of Heike warriors, a jealous Rokujo and a fisherman-turned-angel return to chant their sorrows to wandering priests. Framed by a long introduction on the masks, music and Buddhist outlook of the stage.

books.title: The Spirit of Japanese Art
books.author: Yoné Noguchi
books.synopsis: Noguchi profiles Japanese artists from Koyetsu and Utamaro to the madcap Kyosai and the Turner-loving Hara, arguing that kokoromochi, the spirit behind the brush, matters more than technique. He mixes anecdotes, tea-room visits and comparisons with Whistler and Western painters.
